name: Hammerfall

angles.text: For the Horde, Hammerfall recalls the liberation of the orcish internment camps and Warchief Orgrim Doomhammer's sacrifice.
For orcs, Doomhammer's fall in Arathi remains one of history's most painful moments. It marked the end of an era and the rise of Thrall's new Horde.
As a warrior, you can remember Orgrim Doomhammer as a legendary fighter. The ground where he fell carries the weight of that battle.

faq.answer: Gor'mul was an orc captive at the internment camp where Hammerfall now stands. Thrall and Doomhammer led an assault to free the captives, but Gor'mul was left behind during the escape. He wandered alone in despair for years.
Orgrim Doomhammer died in the battle to free the Arathi internment camp. An Alliance knight on horseback struck him from behind with a lance.
Hammerfall bears the name of Warchief Orgrim Doomhammer, who fell there while freeing his people from human captivity. The Horde returned to the ruined camp and made it a permanent base.
faq.q: Why is the outpost named Hammerfall?

faq.answer: Tor'gan is a Horde representative stationed at Hammerfall. He helps care for the encampment and understands the lingering trauma of former captives like Gor'mul.
Yes. Thrall fought beside Warchief Orgrim Doomhammer in the assault on the Arathi internment camp. They broke its defenses and freed captive orcs, but Doomhammer died in the battle.
faq.q: Did Thrall take part in the battle here?

faq.answer: Gor'mul watched Doomhammer fall, and the sight crushed his spirit. When the other captives escaped into the wilderness, Gor'mul was left behind to wander without hope until the Horde returned to build Hammerfall.

sections.body: In the Arathi Highlands, the Alliance once held orcs captive behind wood and steel. Young Thrall and Warchief Orgrim Doomhammer led an assault on the camp's enclosures and freed their kin. Many captives escaped as the defenses fell. Then a mounted lance struck Doomhammer from behind. He died where Hammerfall now stands.
sections.title: Blood and Broken Chains

sections.body: Gor'mul was among those who did not find freedom that day. In the battle's chaos and the earth's tremors, he watched the Warchief fall and lost the will to fight. His brethren fled, leaving him behind. For years, Gor'mul wandered the highlands in grief. The Horde has reclaimed the site as a fortified base, yet survivors still carry the memory of Doomhammer's death.
sections.title: The Lingering Shadow of Defeat

summary: At Hammerfall, the Horde holds a camp won at the cost of Warchief Orgrim Doomhammer's life. Gor'mul remembers the captives' escape and why the stronghold bears its name.
